children: SYDNEY--Ampol said its third-quarter earnings rose as refining margins stayed strong against a backdrop of heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and ongoing tightness in fuel supply.

Ampol said earnings before interest and tax in three months through September increased compared to the quarterly average for the second half of 2025 when measured on a replacement cost-of-sales basis, which strips out the impact of movements in oil prices by restating the cost of sales using the replacement cost of goods sold.
Ampol reported a Lytton Refiner Margin of US$23.92 per barrel for the quarter, which was more than double its level of a year ago.
Ampol said the strength in refinery margins was achieved despite the company carrying out major maintenance work at its Lytton refinery in eastern Australia's Queensland state during the period.

Management said it now intends to bring forward additional maintenance of one of the refinery's crude units, which would reduce production of higher-value products such as gasoline and jet fuel by some 150 million liters in the fourth quarter.
Ampol said its third-quarter earnings demonstrated the strength of its integrated supply chain and benefited from favorable operating conditions.

Headline shop sales in its Convenience Retail business rose by a double-digit percent compared with a year earlier when its U-GO unstaffed sites and the recently acquired EG Australia business are excluded.
"Retail fuel margins were broadly in line with 3Q 2025, despite a rising fuel input cost environment, reflecting Ampol's supply arrangements, product mix and channel mix," the company said.
Ampol said initial integration of the EG Australia business is progressing to plan and management is increasingly confident in meeting savings targets from the deal.
Ampol added that it now expects to commission the Ultra Low Sulfur Fuels project at Lytton in the first quarter of next year, but this change isn't expected to have a material impact on earnings.
